baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Dispossessed Lives (2016) studies the production of archival silence and changes the narrative gaze toward enslaved women, while refusing a claim of complete recovery.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: The publisher-authorized book excerpt and interview, read, support the method; the 2010 abstract supplies an earlier distinct challenge to triumphalist representations of Polgreen. The whole book remains unread; unnamed objections are Fuentes’s report, not independently read replies.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: With Deborah Gray White and a collective of researchers, Scarlet and Black (2016) brings Rutgers’s involvement in slavery and dispossession into the university’s public history.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Publisher description and contents, read, establish a jointly edited committee publication with separately named chapter authors. White wrote its introduction; Fuentes is neither sole author nor sole discoverer. Contribution is scoped to this collaborative publication and stated public purpose, not a general claim to founding public history.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Hartman’s “Venus in Two Acts” is explicitly named as inspiration for Connolly and Fuentes’s 2016 slavery/archive special issue, as Fuentes reports in 2017.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Fuentes’s AAIHS essay explicitly identifies Hartman’s essay as inspiration. Fuentes’s author bibliography establishes Connolly’s coeditorship and 2016; USF corroborates their joint introduction in Fall 2016. Influence is limited to that collaborative project, not Hartman as sole source of Fuentes’s work or agreement on every method. The full issue remains unread.

relevant_group_routes.relationship: The archive of Atlantic slavery as the field's hardest case: Hartman's 'Venus in Two Acts' (2008) and the 'critical fabulation' the MacArthur Foundation describes (2019); Fuentes's Dispossessed Lives (2016), which 'interrogates the archive and its historical production' for Bridgetown's enslaved and free women (publisher)
relevant_group_routes.evidence_note: MacArthur's description of critical fabulation (read); Fuentes's publisher description (read). Hartman and Fuentes unread. Trouillot's clauses were removed after review (finding 9): p4A_rel_21 carries them.

relevant_group_routes.relationship: Hartman's 'critical fabulation' and Fuentes's black-feminist reading of 'fragmentary sources' (2016) take the archive's violence as the problem of Black history
relevant_group_routes.evidence_note: MacArthur's description (read); Fuentes's publisher description (read). The black entry's strand archives ('Collecting and diaspora bibliography') is the hook. Trouillot's clause was removed after review (finding 9): p4A_rel_25 carries it.
